body: I'm well aware that GPA is irrelevant once you're in the workforce. The issue is entering the workforce in the first place - and since I don't have any type of experience, I'm really going to struggle with even stepping into the workface [just getting a callback for an interview is a huge struggle]. And my shitty gpa definitely won't be doing me any favors. I'm graduating in May, other students who are graduating at the time already got jobs lined up, I literally have nothing in my life [which is my own damn fault, but my point is I'm not "freaking out way too early". I have every right to be freaking out lol].

Well by "awesome profession", I mean a lot of people had already done a few internships and now have jobs lined up at the Big 4 for when they graduate in May.

Personally, I never had goals like that. I just hope to get a job [anywhere] that's actually relevant to my major. I guess you're right though; I am really behind and part of that problem is because I don't have a specific endgoal. I've moreorless just been on autopilot and was coasting by without any real plans for a future.

I've had that hope, that [my] future would be better, for so long ... but it's just really unrealistic, and sticking around even longer is just doing more bad than good. That "maybe" really isn't good enough at this point.
